d: used to say yes politely or to show something is obvious
ex: Can I sit here? "Of course."

d: used to explain or correct what you just said
ex: It was cheap. I mean, not cheap, but good value.
exTr: Ucuzdu. Yani ucuz değil ama fiyatına değerdi.
exAr: كان رخيصًا. أعني، ليس رخيصًا، لكنه يستحق سعره.

d: used while you think, or to check the listener understands
ex: He's a bit, you know, shy with new people.
exTr: O biraz, bilirsin, yeni insanlarla utangaç.
exAr: إنه، كما تعلم، خجول قليلًا مع الناس الجدد.

d: used to add something not connected to the main topic
ex: By the way, Sara called while you were out.
exTr: Bu arada, sen dışarıdayken Sara aradı.
exAr: بالمناسبة، اتصلت سارة وأنت في الخارج.

d: used to say you are happy to help, or after someone thanks you
ex: Thanks for the lift. "No problem."

d: used to tell someone not to worry, or that something is not important
ex: Never mind, we can take the next bus.
exTr: Boş ver, bir sonraki otobüse bineriz.
exAr: لا يهم، يمكننا ركوب الحافلة التالية.

d: not less than; used to say something is good despite a problem
ex: The hotel was small, but at least it was clean.
exTr: Otel küçüktü ama en azından temizdi.
exAr: كان الفندق صغيرًا، لكنه على الأقل كان نظيفًا.

d: used to give one thing that shows what you mean
ex: Some fruits, for example oranges, have a lot of vitamin C.
exTr: Bazı meyveler, örneğin portakal, çok C vitamini içerir.
exAr: بعض الفواكه، على سبيل المثال البرتقال، فيها الكثير من فيتامين سي.

d: a large amount or number of
ex: We have a lot of work this week.
exTr: Bu hafta bir sürü işimiz var.
exAr: لدينا الكثير من العمل هذا الأسبوع.

d: a little; in some way (informal)
ex: I'm kind of tired, so I'll stay home tonight.
exTr: Biraz yorgunum, o yüzden bu akşam evde kalacağım.
exAr: أنا متعب نوعًا ما، لذلك سأبقى في البيت الليلة.

d: a little; not exactly (informal)
ex: It's sort of a café and a bookshop together.
exTr: Bir çeşit kafe ve kitapçı bir arada.
exAr: إنه ما يشبه مقهى ومكتبة معًا.

d: also, too (usually at the end of a sentence)
ex: I'd like a coffee, and a sandwich as well.
exTr: Bir kahve istiyorum, bir de sandviç.

d: used to add something true and often surprising
ex: He isn't lazy. In fact, he works two jobs.
exTr: O tembel değil. Aslında iki işte çalışıyor.
exAr: ليس كسولًا. في الواقع، يعمل في وظيفتين.

d: used to say yes when you are not completely sure
ex: Is the shop open today? "I think so."

d: used to say no politely, or when you are not sure
ex: Is it going to rain? "I don't think so."

d: used to say you want something to be true
ex: Will you pass the exam? "I hope so!"

d: used to say the answer changes with the situation
ex: Do you walk to work? "It depends on the weather."
exAr: هل تمشي إلى العمل؟ "يعتمد على الطقس."

d: used to say something is correct
ex: You're from Izmir? "That's right."

d: used to say something is finished, or that you found the answer
ex: Sign here, and that's it. You're done.
exTr: Buraya imza at, bu kadar. Bitti.
exAr: وقّع هنا، وهذا كل شيء. انتهيت.

d: used to make a suggestion
ex: How about pizza tonight?

d: used to suggest something or ask about another person or thing
ex: I'm having tea. What about you?

d: tell me (when you have the information)
ex: Let me know if you need any help.
exTr: Yardıma ihtiyacın olursa bana haber ver.

d: used when saying goodbye; be careful
ex: See you tomorrow. Take care!

d: goodbye (informal)
ex: See you on Monday!

d: used to get attention politely, or to say sorry for a small thing
ex: Excuse me, is this seat free?

d: used to say something bad or disappointing politely
ex: I'm afraid we're closed today.

d: I would prefer to
ex: I'd rather stay in than go to the party.
exTr: Partiye gitmektense evde kalmayı tercih ederim.
exAr: أفضّل البقاء في البيت على الذهاب إلى الحفلة.

d: I want to (polite)
ex: I'd like to book a table for two.
exTr: İki kişilik bir masa ayırtmak istiyorum.

d: used to offer something politely
ex: Would you like some more tea?

d: used to ask for permission politely
ex: Do you mind if I open the window?

d: used to ask someone politely to do something
ex: Would you mind closing the door?

d: used to ask for something very politely
ex: I was wondering if you could help me with this form.
exTr: Acaba bu formda bana yardım edebilir misiniz diye merak ediyordum.
exAr: كنت أتساءل إن كان بإمكانك مساعدتي في هذا النموذج.

d: used to ask politely
ex: Could you speak a bit more slowly, please?
exTr: Biraz daha yavaş konuşabilir misiniz, lütfen?
exAr: هل يمكنك أن تتكلم ببطء أكثر من فضلك؟

d: you can decide
ex: We can eat in or go out. It's up to you.
exTr: Evde yiyebiliriz ya da dışarı çıkabiliriz. Sana kalmış.
exAr: يمكننا الأكل في البيت أو الخروج. الأمر يعود إليك.

d: used to say strongly no, or that you are surprised
ex: He ran 40 kilometres? "No way!"

d: it is not surprising
ex: You didn't sleep last night. No wonder you're tired.
exTr: Dün gece uyumadın. Yorgun olmana şaşmamalı.
exAr: لم تنم البارحة. لا عجب أنك متعب.

d: used to show surprise
ex: I can't believe it's already December.
exAr: لا أصدق أننا في ديسمبر بالفعل.

d: I don't know at all
ex: Where are my keys? "I have no idea."

d: it is not important
ex: It doesn't matter if you're late. Just come.
exTr: Geç kalman önemli değil. Sadece gel.
exAr: لا يهم إن تأخرت. فقط تعال.

d: how are you, or what is the problem (informal)
ex: Hey, what's up? You look worried.

d: how are you (informal)
ex: Hi Tom, how's it going?

d: quite good
ex: How was the film? "Not bad."

d: I also feel or do the same
ex: I'm hungry. "Me too."

d: I also don't
ex: I don't like horror films. "Me neither."

d: I also do (after a positive sentence)
ex: I love this song. "So do I."

d: I also don't (after a negative sentence)
ex: I don't eat meat. "Neither do I."

d: used to wish someone success
ex: Good luck with your interview tomorrow!

d: used to praise someone
ex: You passed! Well done!

d: wait a moment (informal)
ex: Hang on, I'll get my coat.

d: please wait a short time
ex: Just a moment, I'll check for you.
exTr: Bir dakika, sizin için kontrol edeyim.

d: used when you give something to someone
ex: Can I have the menu? "Here you are."

d: used to give permission or tell someone to start
ex: Can I use your phone? "Sure, go ahead."

d: used to let someone go first politely
ex: After you. "Oh, thank you."

d: check or do something so that something is certain
ex: Make sure you lock the door when you leave.
exAr: تأكّد من قفل الباب عند خروجك.

d: I don't know for certain
ex: I'm not sure what time the train leaves.
exTr: Trenin saat kaçta kalktığından emin değilim.

d: used before saying what you really think
ex: To be honest, I didn't enjoy the meal.

d: from what I know (I may be wrong)
ex: As far as I know, the meeting is still on.
exAr: على حد علمي، الاجتماع ما زال قائمًا.

d: used to give advice
ex: If I were you, I'd take the job.
exTr: Senin yerinde olsam o işi alırdım.

d: you should (or something bad may happen)
ex: You'd better hurry, or you'll miss the bus.
exTr: Acele etsen iyi olur, yoksa otobüsü kaçıracaksın.
exAr: من الأفضل أن تسرع وإلا فاتتك الحافلة.

d: I'm happy and excited about something in the future
ex: The holiday starts on Friday. I'm looking forward to it.
exAr: تبدأ العطلة يوم الجمعة. أنا أتطلع إليها.

d: used to ask someone to explain
ex: What do you mean, the flight is cancelled?

d: what is wrong?
ex: What's the matter? Are you ill?

d: used to check if someone is certain
ex: Are you sure this is the right address?
exTr: Bunun doğru adres olduğundan emin misin?
exAr: هل أنت متأكد أن هذا هو العنوان الصحيح؟

d: it is sad or disappointing
ex: It's a pity you can't come to the wedding.
exAr: من المؤسف أنك لا تستطيع حضور الزفاف.

d: how sad or disappointing
ex: The concert was cancelled. "What a shame!"

d: used to tell someone to feel happier
ex: Cheer up! It's only one bad mark.
exAr: ابتهج! إنها مجرد علامة سيئة واحدة.

d: used to tell someone to become less angry or upset
ex: Calm down and tell me what happened.
exTr: Sakin ol ve bana ne olduğunu anlat.

d: be careful (there is danger)
ex: Watch out! There's a car coming.

d: used to encourage someone, or to show you don't believe them
ex: Come on, you can do it!

d: used to accept what someone said as reasonable
ex: I can't come; I have to work. "Fair enough."

d: it is not important; don't worry
ex: You forgot? It's not a big deal.
exTr: Unuttun mu? Büyütülecek bir şey değil.

d: I understand
ex: The shop moved to the next street. "Oh, I see."
exAr: انتقل المتجر إلى الشارع المجاور. "آه، فهمت."

d: I understand (informal)
ex: Turn left, then right. "Got it, thanks."
exTr: Sola, sonra sağa dön. "Anladım, sağ ol."

d: used to agree with a plan
ex: Let's meet at six. "Sounds good."

d: used after someone thanks you
ex: Thank you so much. "You're welcome."

d: no; or a polite answer to thanks
ex: Am I disturbing you? "Not at all."

d: OK; acceptable; not hurt
ex: Is everything all right? You look pale.
exTr: Her şey yolunda mı? Solgun görünüyorsun.
exAr: هل كل شيء على ما يرام؟ تبدو شاحبًا.

d: used when someone tells you bad news
ex: My grandmother is in hospital. "I'm sorry to hear that."

d: used to say you are happy about someone's success
ex: Congratulations on your new job!

d: I am responsible for the mistake
ex: Don't blame her. It's my fault.

d: used to say you were happy to help
ex: Thanks for dinner. "My pleasure."
exTr: Akşam yemeği için teşekkürler. "Benim için zevkti."

d: used when you meet someone for the first time
ex: Hi, I'm Ali. Nice to meet you.
exTr: Merhaba, ben Ali. Tanıştığımıza memnun oldum.

d: used when you meet someone after a long time (informal)
ex: Maria! Long time no see! How are you?
exTr: Maria! Görüşmeyeli uzun zaman oldu! Nasılsın?
exAr: ماريا! زمان لم نلتقِ! كيف حالك؟

d: don't hurry
ex: Take your time. We're not in a rush.

d: take what you want (food, drink) freely
ex: There's coffee in the kitchen. Help yourself.
exAr: هناك قهوة في المطبخ. تفضّل وخذ.

d: relax and behave as if this were your home
ex: Come in and make yourself at home.
exTr: Gel içeri, kendi evin gibi rahat ol.

d: how sad or disappointing
ex: I lost the photos. "Oh, what a pity."

d: I am coming now
ex: I'm on my way. I'll be there in ten minutes.
exAr: أنا في الطريق. سأصل خلال عشر دقائق.

d: I am very excited about something in the future
ex: We fly to Rome tomorrow. I can't wait!
exAr: نسافر إلى روما غدًا. لا أطيق الانتظار!

d: it is fine for me; I have no problem with it
ex: I don't mind waiting. Take your time.
exTr: Beklemek benim için sorun değil. Acele etme.

d: it will not help
ex: It's no use calling him. His phone is off.
exTr: Onu aramanın faydası yok. Telefonu kapalı.
exAr: لا فائدة من الاتصال به. هاتفه مغلق.

d: it is useless to do something
ex: There's no point in waiting. The shop is closed.
exAr: لا جدوى من الانتظار. المتجر مغلق.

d: it is useful or good enough to do
ex: The museum is small, but it's worth a visit.

d: now is the moment to do something
ex: It's time to go home.

d: what is the problem?
ex: What's wrong with your car?

d: I am certain
ex: I'm sure you'll do well in the test.
exAr: أنا متأكد أنك ستبلي جيدًا في الامتحان.

d: because something might happen
ex: Take an umbrella, just in case.
exTr: Her ihtimale karşı bir şemsiye al.

d: in the way that usually happens
ex: As usual, the bus was late.
exTr: Her zamanki gibi otobüs geç kaldı.

d: used to change the topic or return to the main point
ex: Anyway, let's talk about the plan.
exAr: على أي حال، لنتحدث عن الخطة.

d: used before saying something surprising
ex: Believe it or not, I've never seen the sea.
exTr: İster inan ister inanma, denizi hiç görmedim.
exAr: صدّق أو لا تصدّق، لم أرَ البحر قط.
